decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep its benchmark interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continue its asset purchase program.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its description of economic growth from a modest pace earlier in the year to a moderate pace.

changes.quote: Some indicators of labor market conditions have shown further improvement in recent months, but the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: The Fed adjusted its phrasing to specify that some job market indicators improved, while the overall unemployment rate remains high.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has been strengthening, but mortgage rates have risen further and fiscal policy is restraining economic growth.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that mortgage rates have risen further, adding to the headwinds from federal fiscal policy.

changes.quote: Taking into account the extent of federal fiscal retrenchment, the Committee sees the improvement in economic activity and labor market conditions since it began its asset purchase program a year ago as consistent with growing underlying strength in the broader economy.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to acknowledge that the economy has grown stronger over the past year despite government spending cuts.

changes.quote: However, the Committee decided to await more evidence that progress will be sustained before adjusting the pace of its purchases.
changes.explanation: The Fed explained that it wants to see more proof of ongoing economic progress before it slows down its bond-buying program.

tone_quotes.quote: Apart from fluctuations due to changes in energy prices, inflation has been running below the Committee's longer-run objective, but longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
However, the Committee decided to await more evidence that progress will be sustained before adjusting the pace of its purchases.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.95% APR costs about $49.79 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.69% and moved -17 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.57% would fall by about $30.28 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.2%, and employers added an average of 183k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.5% over the past year (August 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will continue its bond purchases and low interest rates until it sees further sustained improvement in the job market. Educational forecast models suggest an 81% probability of a hold at upcoming meetings.

citations.detail: In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent
